release.name: The Hunt for Stanley 2026 Encore Pack
release.description:
Sale Starts: Thursday July 9 at 1PM ET / 10AM PT

 

Price: $12 USD

# Packs Available: 1000 packs total. Edition numbers are distributed randomly upon purchase.

 

Purchase Limit: Ten (10) pack limit per person for the first 6 hours; the limit increases to a fifty (50) pack limit per person afterward. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 5

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • One (1) highlight from The Hunt for Stanley 2026 (Limited #/500)
  • Two (2) highlights with the following probabilities:
    • 20% Base 2025-26 (Core #/1500)
    • 50% The Hunt for Stanley 2026 (Limited #/500)
    • 30% Opening Ice 2025-26 (Rare #/250)
  • One (1) highlight  with the following probabilities:
    • 25% The Hunt for Stanley 2026 (Limited #/500)
    • 25% Filthy Apples (Limited #/500)
    • 25% Next-Gen Class 2025-26 (Limited #/500)
    • 25% Base 2025-26 (Core #/1500)
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 19.6% Playoff Bound 2026 (Core #/1500)
    • 50% Base 2025-26 (Core #/1500)
    • 25% Opening Ice 2025-26 (Rare #/250)
    • 5% Making the Mark 2025-26 (Epic #/100)
    • 0.2% The Greatest Achievements (Legendary #/10)
    • 0.2% Ice Vault (Mythic #/1) 

Highlights List

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be processed via Stripe. 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights are eligible to be sold to other collectors in the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace. See FAQ.

Transferability: Packs and highlights can be exchanged in the Trade Lounge™ with other NHL Breakaway users.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

Sets Included:

  • The Hunt for Stanley 2026 - Preview 
  • Playoff Bound 2026 - Preview
  • Base 2025-26, Series 3 - Preview
  • Filthy Apples - Preview
  • Next-Gen Class 2025-26 - Preview 
  • Opening Ice 2025-26, Series 3 - Preview
  • Making the Mark 2025-26 - Preview 
  • The Greatest Achievements, Series 3 - Preview

 

Collection Guarantee: Series 3 highlights will only be distributed during Series 3, which ends prior to the start of the 2026-27 Regular Season. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

summary.name: Logan Stankoven
summary.description:
In Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Final, Logan Stankoven — who had already scored game-winning goals in the previous rounds — delivered his third playoff game-winner of the postseason to help the Carolina Hurricanes close out the series against the Montreal Canadiens.  
Receiving a pass from Taylor Hall behind the net, the young forward snapped a shot from the right circle that beat the goaltender over the left shoulder in the first period, pushing Carolina ahead 2-0. Stankoven’s tally was part of a dominant opening frame in which the Hurricanes scored three times and never looked back.  
The goal helped spark a 6-1 victory that eliminated Montreal in five games and sent Carolina to the Stanley Cup Final.

summary.name: Jack Eichel
summary.description:
"In the third period of Game 2 in the Western Conference Final, Jack Eichel delivered the tying goal that ignited a comeback for the Vegas Golden Knights on the road against the Colorado Avalanche.  
Trailing 1-0 midway through the frame and still without a goal in the contest, Eichel took a pass from Ivan Barbashev, touched by Pavel Dorofeyev, on the rush, slowed in the right circle, and fired a shot past the goaltender inside the left post to tie the score at 1-1.  
Eichel’s timely tally was Vegas’ first of the game and sparked a comeback win. The Golden Knights 3-1 victory secured a 2-0 series lead which began on the road in Colorado. Vegas would go on to sweep the series against the Presidents’ Trophy-winning Avalanche."

summary.name: Jackson Blake
summary.description:
In overtime of Game 4 in the Eastern Conference Second Round, Jackson Blake delivered the series-clinching goal that swept the Philadelphia Flyers and sent the Carolina Hurricanes to the Eastern Conference Final.  
Tied 2-2 in the extra frame, Blake received a pass from Taylor Hall near the top of the circles. The right winger, who had already found the net once in regulation, settled the puck before ripping a wrist shot from the slot that found the net.  
Blake's first career playoff overtime goal completed the four-game sweep and kept Carolina's remarkable postseason momentum rolling into the Eastern Conference Final.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Carter Hart
summary.description:
In Game 6 of the second round on the road against the Anaheim Ducks, with a chance to clinch the series on the line, Carter Hart flashed the glove with a brilliant save midway through the third period.
The netminder stood tall the rest of the way, turning aside 31 of 32 shots to allow just one goal and eliminate the Ducks. Across the second round series, Hart posted a .935 save percentage and a 1.99 goals-against average.

summary.name: Nathan MacKinnon
summary.description:
In the final minutes of the third period in Game 5 of the Western Conference Second Round, Nathan MacKinnon delivered a clutch tying goal that forced overtime against the Minnesota Wild.  
Trailing 3-2 with 1:23 remaining, MacKinnon took a feed and ripped a wrist shot from a tight angle under the left dot. The puck beat the goaltender top shelf short side, finding the smallest opening to knot the score at 3-3 and complete Colorado’s comeback from three goals down.  
MacKinnon’s strike sent the game to overtime, where the Avalanche would go on to win and clinch the series in five games.

summary.name: Alex Newhook
summary.description:
In overtime of Game 7 in the Eastern Conference Second Round, Alex Newhook once again played the hero for the Montreal Canadiens.  
With the score tied 2-2 against the Buffalo Sabres, Newhook took a cross-ice pass from Alexandre Carrier and skated to the top of the left circle. The forward wired a low wrist shot that beat the goaltender glove side at 11:22 of the extra frame.  
Newhook’s overtime winner completed a 3-2 victory that eliminated the Sabres and advanced Montreal to the Eastern Conference Final. It was his second Game 7 series-clinching goal of the playoffs, following the game-winner he scored in the third period of the first-round clincher against the Tampa Bay Lightning.

summary.name: Wayne Gretzky
summary.description:
On December 30, 1981, Wayne Gretzky delivered a performance for the ages, etching his name even deeper into hockey history. Facing the Philadelphia Flyers at Northlands Coliseum, Gretzky erupted for an incredible five-goal night, reaching the unprecedented milestone of 50 goals in just 39 games. Each goal told a story: his first two came in the opening period to set the tone, his third helped Edmonton reclaim a two-goal advantage in the second, his fourth—the game-winning goal—highlighted his clutch play, and his fifth, an empty-netter with seconds remaining, sent the Edmonton Oilers faithful into a frenzy as "The Great One" shattered the NHL’s previous record of 50 goals in 50 games.  
At just 20 years old, Gretzky’s achievement showcased his unparalleled scoring ability, vision, and dominance over the game. That season, he would go on to set a staggering 92-goal record, solidifying his place as one of hockey's most extraordinary talents. Gretzky’s 50-in-39 remains a defining moment in the sport’s history—a feat that redefined the limits of greatness and further established his legacy as a generational icon.

summary.name: Patrick Kane
summary.description:
Patrick Kane’s Stanley Cup–clinching goal in 2010 was one of the most unforgettable moments in NHL history—chaotic, dramatic, and entirely fitting for a player known for flair under pressure. In overtime of Game 6 against the Philadelphia Flyers, Kane collected the puck near the left boards, accelerated down the wing, and slipped a sharp-angle shot between Michael Leighton’s pads. The puck quietly lodged itself beneath the padding at the back of the net, going unnoticed by nearly everyone in the arena—except Kane.  
Without hesitation, he threw his gloves in the air and skated toward center ice, celebrating what he instantly knew was the goal that would deliver the Chicago Blackhawks their first Stanley Cup in 49 years. The officials needed a video review to confirm what Kane already did: he had just made history. At only 21 years old, Kane became the youngest player ever to score an overtime goal to win the Stanley Cup, cementing his status as a clutch performer and etching his name into NHL lore.

summary.description:
Ice Vault is NHL Breakaway’s premier Mythic-tier collectible set.
It contains only the highest-rarity highlights, with each piece limited to fewer than 10 editions. Every highlight receives unique Mythic visual styling and custom framing reserved exclusively for this tier.
Once a highlight enters the Ice Vault, it is permanently retired and never released in any other set or edition.
